Cell-level linear mixed model sc-ExWAS with finite-df inference

Source: R/glmm-inference.R
run_sc_exwas_glmm.Rd

Fits, per gene, the cell-level model y ~ exposure * celltype + covariates + (1 | donor) + (1 | donor:celltype) and reports cell-type-specific exposure effects. For family = "gaussian" the model is a linear mixed model fitted by lmerTest::lmer with REML = TRUE (mandatory), and p-values are referred to a finite denominator degrees of freedom – Satterthwaite (default) or Kenward-Roger – via lmerTest::contest1D. A Wald test referred to the normal distribution would be anticonservative with few donors.

Usage

run_sc_exwas_glmm(
  x,
  exposure,
  celltype_col = "cell_type",
  covariates = NULL,
  target_genes = NULL,
  ddf = c("Satterthwaite", "Kenward-Roger"),
  family = c("gaussian", "nbinom"),
  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)

Arguments

x

A SingleCellExposomeExperiment. Each cell's donor is read from the colData column named by sampleColumn(x).

exposure

Character; a donor-level column of exposureData(x).

celltype_col

Character. Column in colData containing cell type annotations. Default "cell_type".

covariates

Character vector; donor covariate columns in exposureData (numeric), added as fixed-effect main effects. The names exposure, donor, celltype and y are used by the model and cannot be covariate names; with family = "nbinom" the same holds for logoff and the expo_<cell type> columns. Each name must be a syntactic R name (see make.names) other than ., ... and names such as ..1, which R reads specially in a formula, and the exposure itself cannot be a covariate.

target_genes

Character; genes to test (default: all rows of x). A cell-level LMM per gene is costly – passing a focused gene set is strongly recommended.

ddf

Denominator degrees-of-freedom method for family = "gaussian": "Satterthwaite" (default) or "Kenward-Roger" (needs pbkrtest; use for \(n \lesssim 30\) donors).

family

"gaussian" (LMM on cell-level \(\log_2\) CP10k, default) or "nbinom" (negative-binomial GLMM on cell counts).

BPPARAM

A BiocParallel param used to parallelise over genes. Defaults to BiocParallel::SerialParam(), so no worker process is started unless one is asked for; pass, for example, BiocParallel::SnowParam(workers = 2L) to fit genes in parallel.

Value

A DataFrame, one row per gene x cell type: gene, celltype, log2FC, se, statistic (Satterthwaite /KR \(t\) for gaussian, LR \(\chi^2\) for nbinom), df (finite denominator df; 1 for the nbinom LRT), pvalue, padj_global (BH across all gene-by-cell-type strata, as in run_sc_exwas; there is no within-cell-type padj), and method. Rows ordered by padj_global, then pvalue. A gene-by-cell-type stratum that cannot be fitted is left out of the result; with family = "nbinom", a stratum whose likelihood-ratio test cannot be computed is kept with NA pvalue and padj_global. Its statistic is NA when the reduced model or anova() fails, and close to 0 when the test has no degrees of freedom, as when a covariate is a linear function of the exposure. padj_global adjusts over the strata with a p-value, and the function stops when no stratum can be fitted.

Details

Why REML. Maximum likelihood biases the variance components downward, which shrinks the residual scale and inflates the exposure \(t\)-statistic; the Kenward-Roger adjusted covariance and the Satterthwaite degrees-of-freedom approximation are both defined only on the REML fit. The function therefore forces REML = TRUE and does not expose a switch.

Random effects. The exposure varies between donors, so the replicates for a cell-type-specific exposure effect are donor-by-cell-type units, not cells. The model therefore includes a donor-by-cell-type random intercept as well as a donor random intercept; without it, variation shared by the cells of one donor and cell type is treated as independent and the cell-type-specific tests are anticonservative. With a single cell type the model reduces to y ~ exposure + covariates + (1 | donor). A variance component estimated at zero (a singular fit) is expected when that source of variation is absent and is not reported.

Cell-type-specific effects. Under treatment contrasts the exposure coefficient is the effect at the reference cell type and each exposure:celltype coefficient is a difference from it. Each cell type's effect is therefore a linear combination of fixed effects, tested with contest1D so that the degrees of freedom and standard error account for the covariance between the main effect and the interaction.

family = "nbinom". Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger are linear -mixed-model constructions and do not extend to a generalised LMM, so the negative-binomial path fits lme4::glmer.nb on an equivalent cell-type-nested reparametrisation of exposure * celltype (one exposure slope column per cell type) and tests each cell type's effect by a likelihood-ratio test (anova of the full versus the column-dropped model) – again not a Wald-normal test. This path is markedly more expensive (one glmer.nb refit per cell type per gene); for count data prefer the donor-level run_sc_exwas_pb_offset, which is calibration- equivalent and far faster (Lee & Han 2024). The ddf argument is ignored for family = "nbinom".

Missing values. The cells of a donor whose exposure or a covariate is missing, and cells without a cell-type label, are left out, with a message, before either family is fitted, so that the full and reduced models of a likelihood-ratio test use the same cells.

Note

Calibrate against a donor-permutation null, with the exposure permuted across donors, before quoting any type-I rate; Satterthwaite/KR control the finite-sample error only under the working model, so the empirical check is the headline.

References

Kuznetsova A, Brockhoff PB & Christensen RHB (2017). lmerTest package: tests in linear mixed effects models. J Stat Softw 82(13).

Kenward MG & Roger JH (1997). Small sample inference for fixed effects from restricted maximum likelihood. Biometrics 53:983-997.

Halekoh U & Hojsgaard S (2014). A Kenward-Roger approximation and parametric bootstrap methods for tests in linear mixed models – the R package pbkrtest. J Stat Softw 59(9).

See also

run_sc_exwas_pb_offset for the donor-level default.

Examples

donor_ids <- paste0("D", seq_len(10L))
exposure <- rep(c(0, 1), each = 5L)
cell_donor <- rep(donor_ids, each = 12L)
cell_type <- rep(
    rep(c("TypeA", "TypeB"), each = 6L),
    times = length(donor_ids)
)
cell_ids <- paste0("cell", seq_along(cell_donor))
counts <- outer(
    seq_len(2L),
    seq_along(cell_ids),
    function(gene, cell) 2L + ((7L * gene + 5L * cell) %% 11L)
)
exposed_type_a <- exposure[match(cell_donor, donor_ids)] == 1 &
    cell_type == "TypeA"
counts[1L, exposed_type_a] <- counts[1L, exposed_type_a] + 3L
storage.mode(counts) <- "integer"
dimnames(counts) <- list(c("G1", "G2"), cell_ids)
sce <- SingleCellExperiment::SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = counts),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        cell_id = cell_ids,
        donor_id = cell_donor,
        cell_type = cell_type
    )
)
donor_design <- matrix(exposure, ncol = 1L,
    dimnames = list(donor_ids, "exposure"))
scee <- build_scee(sce, donor_design, sample_col = "donor_id")
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE) &&
        requireNamespace("lmerTest", quietly = TRUE)) {
    mixed_result <- run_sc_exwas_glmm(
        scee,
        exposure = "exposure",
        celltype_col = "cell_type",
        target_genes = "G1",
        family = "gaussian",
        BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
    )
    mixed_result
}
#> DataFrame with 2 rows and 9 columns
#>          gene    celltype    log2FC        se statistic        df    pvalue
#>   <character> <character> <numeric> <numeric> <numeric> <numeric> <numeric>

#> 2          G1       TypeA 0.0863299  0.170915  0.505104       116 0.6144439
#>   padj_global                 method
#>     <numeric>            <character>
#> 1    0.146657 lmerTest/Satterthwaite
#> 2    0.614444 lmerTest/Satterthwaite
